chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem narrated from his father, who narrated that Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad narrated from Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Zayd, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) saying:

A man will emerge from the descendants of my son Musa, whose name is the name of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and he will be buried in the land of Tus, which is in Khorasan. He will be killed there by poison, and will be buried there as a stranger. Whoever visits him, knowing his right, God, the Mighty and Exalted, will grant him the reward of whoever spent and fought before the Conquest.

key_terms.أَجْرَ مَنْ أَنْفَقَ قَبْلَ الْفَتْحِ: The reward of those who spent [in charity] before the Conquest (of Mecca)
key_terms.أَرْضِ طُوسَ: The land of Tus (a city in Khorasan)
key_terms.عَارِفاً بِحَقِّهِ: Knowing his right (acknowledging his spiritual authority)
key_terms.وُلْدِ ابْنِي مُوسَى: Descendants of my son Musa (Imam Musa al-Kazim)

ai.seo_question: Who is the Imam buried in Tus who will be killed by poison, and what is the reward for visiting him?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* specifically identifies Imam Ali al-Rida (a.s.) as the 'man from the progeny of Musa' who was martyred by poison in Tus, establishing the theological basis for the sanctity of his shrine. The promise of reward equating to those who 'spent before the Conquest' (Surah Al-Anfal 8:41) highlights the unique spiritual status of visiting the Imam in his specific place of burial, linking the act of Ziyarah to the highest tier of early Islamic merit.
